ld.description: The Cunneen-Hackett Arts Center features award-winning American painter, sculptor, glass artist and writer Carolyn Schlam in the Victorian Gallery at 9 Vassar Street during their November/December 2026 Art Exhibition Series. Featured will be recent mixed media works, several of which she created at her studio in the Cunneen-Hackett Arts Center, some oils in her visual oxymoron series, and many that are embellished with other materials. She is known for her use of exuberant color, elegant drawing and modern design.

ld.name: Melissa Small Cooper Exhibition at the Cunneen-Hackett Arts Center
ld.description: The Cunneen-Hackett Arts Center presents Hudson Valley based oil painter and educator Melissa Small Cooper in the Reception Gallery at 12 Vassar Street during their November/December 2026 Art Exhibition Series. Her artistic practice is rooted in a profound connection to nature, especially the therapeutic act of caring for flowers and plants. Through the interplay of light, color, and gesture, she aims to honor the idiosyncrasies of flowers and illuminate the quiet beauty in the way we nurture and are nurtured by the world around us.

ld.name: Cristal Ortiz Art Exhibition at the Cunneen-Hackett Arts Center
ld.description: The Cunneen-Hackett Arts Center presents Hudson Valley based contemporary artist Cristal Ortiz in the Hancock Gallery at 12 Vassar Street during their November/December 2026 Art Exhibition Series. Working primarily in small-scale paintings, she explores still life, botanicals, objects, and everyday things that invite a sense of beauty and intimacy through oil, acrylic, and other traditional mediums. Her work is rooted in careful observation and a fascination with the quiet presence of familiar objects, often treating small paintings as spaces for closeness and contemplation.

ld.name: The World of Thomas B. Pope
ld.description: The Newburgh Historical Society's 2026 exhibit focuses on the life and context of Newburgh's Hudson River School painter Thomas B. Pope (1833-1891). This show explores the varied life of Thomas Pope in the rapidly evolving city of Newburgh touching on his life, work, community engagement, as well as his art. Paintings and objects from the Historical Society's collection as well as loans from private collectors will be on display from April to the end of the year.

ld.name: Bruna Esposito: In Light of Facts
ld.description: Opening in the Robert Olnick Pavilion, the exhibition is curated by Nicola Lucchi and marks the first major U.S. presentation of Bruna Esposito's work. Bruna Esposito: In Light of Facts brings together, for the first time in the United States, a substantial selection from the artist's inconveniente (2014) series alongside the immersive installation Oltremare (sotto terra vulnerabili) (2006–2011). Featuring works never before exhibited in the U.S., the exhibition transforms everyday materials into powerful reflections on migration, labor, identity, vulnerability, and the social realities embedded within contemporary systems of movement and exchange.

ld.name: AMERICAN FOLK ART, Fenimore Art Museum, On view April 1 – December 31, 2026
ld.description: Fenimore Art Museum’s folk art collection is one of the nation’s largest and finest. Begun with extensive gifts from Stephen C. Clark, the collection includes a variety of paintings, ship figureheads, quilts, weathervanes, trade signs, cigar-store figures, carvings, and decorated stoneware, all created by American folk artists. The oldest piece in the collection, a seven-foot-long panel on which Hudson River Valley painter John Heaton depicted the Martin Van Bergen farmstead in 1733, is considered to be among the first landscapes ever painted in this country.

ld.name: Peekaboo! Natale Adgnot, Traci Johnson, Lala Abaddon, Lu Walstad, and Song Watkins Park
ld.description: In Peekaboo! each artist considers the past—early memories, religious iconography, monocultural dogma, folklore, kitsch—and how it persists in the present. These remnants of the past hold different weight for each artist, yet for all, they remain significant. Harkening to the concept of object permanence, a developmental milestone where a child comes to understand that something continues to exist even when it is no longer perceptible, the exhibition asks: Do these formative relics continue to exist within us when they are no longer visible? What do we internalize, what do we idolize, and what do we shed?

ld.description: Explore the colorful and imaginative world of pictorial maps in Armchair Traveler: The Pictorial Maps of Michael R. Stone ’80, on view at Tremaine Gallery at The Hotchkiss School from November 3, 2026, through January 24, 2027. Curated by Joan Baldwin, Curator of Special Collections at The Hotchkiss School, the exhibition features a selection of maps from the collection of Hotchkiss alumnus Michael R. Stone ’80. Together, we will make yoga shapes with our bodies, use our imaginations to take a “Yoga Adventure”, play games, learn how to use our breath to calm down, and learn simple, kid-friendly meditation. ld.description:
Experience the timeless music of The Carpenters when Top Of The World comes to Paramount Hudson Valley in Peekskill on March 7, 2027, at 7:00 PM. Celebrated as the world’s premiere Carpenters tribute, this outstanding production is fronted by Debbie Taylor, whose remarkable vocal resemblance to Karen Carpenter captures the warmth, richness, and unmistakable contralto tones that made Karen’s voice so beloved.
Backed by a talented eight-piece ensemble of professional musicians, Debbie and the band recreate the signature sound and intricate arrangements of The Carpenters. Featuring multi-instrumentalists and live performances on keyboards, saxophone, trumpet, flute, and more!

ld.description: Legally Blonde - The Musical – Broadway National Tour.  Based on the iconic movie, Legally Blonde will take you from the sorority house to the halls of justice with Broadway’s brightest heroine and, of course, her Chihuahua, Bruiser. Follow the transformation of Elle Woods as she tackles stereotypes, sexism, snobbery and scandal in pursuit of her dreams, and proves that you can be both legally blonde AND the smartest person in the room. Delighting audiences with memorable songs and explosive dances. Legally Blonde warms the heart by proving that self-discovery never goes out of style!

ld.name: The Simon & Garfunkel Story
ld.description: The Simon & Garfunkel Story is touring North America again this year! Using huge projection photos and original film footage, featuring a full live band performing all the hits including ‘Mrs. Robinson’, ‘Cecilia’, ‘Bridge Over Troubled Water’, ‘Homeward Bound’ and many more. The immersive concert-style theater show chronicles the amazing journey shared by the folk-rock duo, Paul Simon and Art Garfunkel. ld.name: Valerie June
ld.description:
City Winery Hudson Valley presents Valerie June on Wednesday, March 17th at 7:00 PM!

Grammy-nominated singer-songwriter Valerie June has built a devoted following with her distinctive blend of folk, soul, blues, and Americana. Her deeply original songwriting draws from generations of musical tradition while offering a fresh perspective on American roots music.

June’s acclaimed career includes three best-selling solo albums, songwriting for Mavis Staples and The Blind Boys of Alabama, praise from Bob Dylan, and performances alongside John Prine, Norah Jones, Willie Nelson, Brandi Carlile, Robert Plant, and more.

Experience Valerie June live at City Winery Hudson Valley.

ld.name: Sesame Street Live- Elmo's Got The Moves

ld.description:
Director: Noah Segan Run Time: 88 min. Release Year: 2026 
Starring: Giancarlo Esposito, Jamie Lee Curtis, John Turturro, Steve Buscemi, Will Price
Harry Lehman is an aging pickpocket who plies his trade with ever-diminishing returns in a drastically changed New York. Wallets stuffed with cash have been replaced by easily cancelled credit cards, and Harry struggles to make ends meet as he cares for his disabled wife, Rosie. When he unwittingly purloins and fences a valuable USB stick, Harry finds himself in a race against time to return the loot or face the rage of a vengeful crime family.

ld.description:
Amber Rubarth is a singer-songwriter renowned for her raw, soulful voice and poetic songwriting. Former chainsaw sculptor turned self-taught multi-instrumentalist, she has toured her original music extensively across North America, Europe, Japan, and South Africa, performing at esteemed venues such as Carnegie Hall and Glastonbury Festival, and opening for legendary artists including Emmylou Harris, Richie Havens, and Dr. Ralph Stanley.

Her ninth full length album, Cover Crop, is a meditation on our interconnectivity with nature through 15 reimagined songs, self-produced at her cottage in the woods of the Hudson Valley, New York.

ld.name: How to Write a Grant Application Reviewers Want to Fund
ld.description:
In one hour, you will learn how to build an application that is clear, complete, and easy for a reviewer to say yes to.  You will leave with a simple system for tracking deadlines and reusing your best answers, so every application after this one takes less time.

What you will learn:
- What strong applications get right
- How to show reviewers exactly what their money will do
- How to turn your story and numbers into one memorable case
- Walkthrough of a real grant application
- A tracking system that makes each application easier than the last
